issues.legal_issue: The tax status in which beneficiaries derive income from trust property depends on whether the trust instruments confer the property on them individually or as representatives of their Hindu undivided families.
material_facts: The beneficiaries received property and income under trust deeds and initially returned the income for assessment in their individual status, but later claimed it belonged to their respective Hindu undivided families.

The deeds allowed trustees, upon a beneficiary's death before distribution, to use that beneficiary's share for the maintenance of the widow and male issue in the trustees' absolute discretion and to accumulate any surplus to the beneficiary's account.

The deeds provided that, if a beneficiary died before distribution leaving a widow but no son, the widow would receive half the share and the other half would go to the remaining beneficiaries and heirs.

The tax authorities and tribunal assessed the income in the beneficiaries' individual status; the High Court instead held that the property had been received in their capacity as representatives of their Hindu undivided families.
issues.conclusion: The trust deeds intended the property to devolve on the beneficiaries in their individual capacities, so the income was assessable in that status.
issues.legal_principle: The interest conferred by a deed depends on its terms. If the instrument does not clearly describe the interest, the court determines the donor's intention from its language and surrounding circumstances; there is no presumption either way, and each instrument must be construed on its own facts. The discretionary use of a deceased beneficiary's share for family maintenance and the provision reallocating part of the share when the beneficiary leaves only a widow were inconsistent with the property passing to beneficiaries as Kartas of their Hindu undivided families. The Court relied on C.N. Arunachala Mudaliar v. C.A. Muruganatha Mudaliar and Another, [1954] 5 SCR 243. No specific statutory provision was cited.

predicates.income_tax_status_assessment: The proceeding determines the tax status in which income received by beneficiaries from trust property is assessable.
predicates.trustee_discretion_after_death: The trust instrument allows trustees, when a beneficiary dies before distribution, to use the beneficiary's share for the maintenance of the widow and male issue at their discretion and to accumulate any surplus to that beneficiary's account.
predicates.widow_share_reallocation: The trust instrument provides that when a beneficiary dies before distribution leaving a widow but no son, the widow receives part of the share and the remainder is distributed among other beneficiaries and heirs.
predicates.beneficiary_income_assessed_in_individua: The income received by the beneficiary is assessed in the beneficiary's individual status.

issues.definition: When an income-tax assessment concerns income from trust property and the instrument gives trustees discretion over a deceased beneficiary's share and reallocates part of that share when the beneficiary leaves only a widow, the beneficiary's income is assessed in the beneficiary's individual status.
